paragraphs: Friend, this is a heavy one, and I won't pretend otherwise. The LORD tells Moses, "Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites," and Moses calls it "the LORD's vengeance" (Numbers 31:2-3). The walkthrough reminded us that the LORD said the Midianites had deceived Israel in the matter of Peor (Numbers 25:16-18). So the big idea starts here: the LORD takes sin against His people seriously, and He is the One who answers it, not people on their own say-so.

Now look at what happens after the battle. Moses is angry with the officers, and everyone who killed a person or touched the dead has to stay outside the camp for seven days (Numbers 31:14, 19). Then the commanders count their soldiers and say, "not one of us is missing," and they bring gold "to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD" (Numbers 31:49-50). The text puts purifying and atonement right alongside the battle, so I think it is showing us that holiness is real.

Here's what I carry from this, baker: the LORD gave rules for being made clean, and the commanders spoke of atonement before the LORD (Numbers 31:19-24, 50). I think that points to a truth we can hold onto, that coming near to God depends on Him making a way, not on our own record. I know what it's like to be dusty and worn out, and I know it takes Someone else to make a stamper new (Revelation 21:5). Keep your ovens ready, friend, and come to the LORD humble, because He is the One who cleans us up.
